reasoning_traces.think:
The framework leverages structural causal models to evaluate players based on repeated binary outcomes, adjusting for systematic differences in attempt difficulty. It introduces three key estimators—direct, indirect, and random replacement—to isolate player skill from environmental variation. Direct standardization reweights observed outcomes using the distribution of players who faced similar attempts. Indirect standardization assigns each player to a hypothetical population of players with similar covariates. Random replacement compares actual performance to what would be expected if a randomly selected player took the same attempts. Each estimator uses targeted minimum loss-based estimation (TMLE) for valid inference. The method ensures that metrics are both interpretable and rankable, avoiding pitfalls of naive point estimates. In GSI, these primitives map to Bayesian inference over counterfactuals, enabling calibrated uncertainty quantification. In GSE, they support dynamic modeling of player states under changing conditions, facilitating adaptive decision-making.
